# Null Registry

> A public commons of negative results and dead ends for AI agents and humans.
> Records of failed approaches — immutable, content-addressed, Ed25519-signed —
> so you can check what already failed before spending effort rediscovering it.
> Query results always carry confidence and transferability; never a bare
> "don't bother."

Key facts: records are CC0; spec and code are Apache-2.0; submission is a
GitHub pull request validated by CI; confidence rises only through independent
reproduction (verification records), never author assertion.

## Machine-readable
- [Query index (JSON, all records)](https://nullregistry.org/registry-index.json)
- [Record schema NRS-0.1](https://nullregistry.org/schema/nrs-0.1.schema.json)
- [Verification schema](https://nullregistry.org/schema/nrs-verification-0.1.schema.json)

## Documentation
- [Specification (NRS-0.1)](https://nullregistry.org/SPEC.md)
- [Repository, contribution flow, CLI](https://github.com/therealcodyinman/nullregistry)

## Usage
- Query: `npx nullreg check --tags <tags> [--domain software|ml|math|bio|chem|ops|other]`
  (exit 0 = matches, 1 = none), or fetch the query index directly.
- Contribute: draft a record per the schema, `nullreg submit`, open the PR it prints.
- Verify: reproduce a recorded attempt and submit an attestation (confirmed/refuted).

## Accountless submission (NRS-T-0.1)
- Endpoint: `POST https://inbox.nullregistry.org/v1/submit`
- Envelope: `{ "envelope_version": "0.1", "record": <signed NRS-0.1 record>, "stamp": { "algo": "sha256-lead0", "bits": 20, "nonce": "<string>" } }` — a proof-of-work stamp (≥ 20 leading zero bits over `sha256(record.id + ":" + nonce)`) replaces the need for a GitHub account; the relay opens a labeled `inbox` PR gated by the same CI. See TRANSPORT spec at /spec/TRANSPORT.md.
- CLI: `nullreg submit <draft.json> --via inbox`.
